This is such an awesome game, I really enjoyed playing it and would have given it a top rating if it weren't for some issues.
So this is a Rogue-like ( perma-death ) type of game, You start with a character and get to choose between 4 weapons, To start killing monsters to level up and get better equipment as you venture through.
Black Coins dropped by monsters to use in some shops to buy weapons, And some very expensive ones to buy chests that usually have very high leveled stuff.
Fighting style is normal, WASD And space to attack, Although the character just auto attacks when you move forward towards your enemies, If you want keep pressing space to attack repeatedly but it consumes the Stamina.
Caves with power-ups, Shops, Chests and Dungeons all over the map for you to find ( And a few secret places ).
However, In the store page it said that the dungeons are randomly placed around the world, I am pretty sure this is false because I'v been using the guide on steam, To know where to go and in the 4 times I finished the game Its always been exactly the same.
A lot of weapons to get with different charging attacks, Monsters all over the place that spawns back when you leave the screen, And some real awesome set of bosses, The designs in all of it the world and characters is really great.
There aren't potions around the world or anything so you can either heal by the Bonefire (in the first screenshot) Or have a life-steal effect in one of your weapon/armor, And in dungeons some monsters drops a healing potion.
Dungeons are designed to be the ( Rush fast ) Type, With narrowed paths, Not really big and easy to find the door leading to the Dungeon Boss.
The SFX and music in the game are outstanding seriously great job on those.
I don't believe there is a level cap, And a good thing because this game has some sense of Replay-Value so you can play it over and over, Change your character equipment style, Try int or Str or Dex builds, You get Swords, Daggers, Hammers, Axes, Spears, Staffs, Bows, Books and shields, Each with its own stats and they are all randomly generated.
You clearly can see the effect Zelda, Diablo and DarkSouls made on this game and that nostalgic feeling you get while playing it mmmmm yes .. the good ol'days.
So this may all seem so perfect and too good to be true ... well it is, Sadly the game has some upsides that are not completely bad but here goes.
Although the game is very good in all its aspects, But there's the issue of the game being too "short", I can see someone finishing it in 2 hours without using the Map in the guide ( I used it a lot don't judge me)
But I mean really, The game price is reasonable for the time you spend on it.
This is probably the most frustrating thing that got me in the game, The game music are AMAZING And it sucks! Because I couldn't really enjoy them like I hoped to.
You see there are no options to raise the volume, So the sound effects of your movement and attacking and everything, Is higher than the game's music so you barely hear it.
And to make it worse it keeps fading in some places, And becomes muted for a while before starting again.
I think its falsely advertised in the store-page.
I quot "The dungeons are randomly placed in the overworld, changing your experience each play through."
Overworld is the normal world you start in and the one that has the dungeons all over.
But like I said before, I finished the game 4 times and they are always at the same place.
I also died once and restarted a new game and still, They are at the same exact place. ( Check the map in the guide section)
There is the matter of the last achievement, That is stopping me and all players from getting 100%.
Turns out its actually broken, So there is no way for any of us to get 100% which is frustrating, And the game has been around for a while and still no response or update.... this is really disappointing.
There is also the matter of the (Online-Disabled) which appears in the option menu, Apparently they had (or have) plans for it, But its been like this ever since release, Hopefully I will update this and maybe remove it if they ever got through it.
Also it says (Steam Leaderboards ) But there is no way to view it in game, If you want to see it you gotta view it through the (View Stats) tab on steam.
I'v been told its not added (yet) so there is hope for it to come one day, But the delaying is taking too long.
Although the game has some real good looking bosses, I'm afraid they are not as tough as you'd expect them to be.
You can pretty much charge and attack them until they die, If your build is slightly weak you might get killed though.
So having all that said lets tackle the Pros and Cons.
1 - Amazing game design, Great soundtracks and wonderful world and dungeons.
2 - A huge set of weapons and armors, Enemies to kill and bosses to fight.
3 - Good replay-value, High-paced gaming and more stuff to discover.
1 - As mentioned before, Music is great but gets covered up by SFX and no option to edit volume.
2 - Last achievement is broken and you cant get 100% because of it.
3 - I wont complain about the game being short, But I will about it being too easy.
4 - False advertising random placed dungeons, And leaderboards.
Don't fear the Cons, Seriously they are not that big of a deal, The game is still good and such an amazing experience I had while playing this baby.
Tl;DR
The nostalgia value in this game is over the roof, Cheap game so you don't need to think twice before buying it, Really fun to play and to see how far can you go without dying.

One of the most amazing games I have ever played.
The story is a somewhat cliche "My best friend has been kidnapped" idea, but IO made the story so great that any cliche is completely irrelevant, and 47's soft side is definitely shown in the game.
47 retires from retirement and goes back to the Agency to do missions in return for collecting info on his missing friend, and these are some of the most unique, well planned missions in stealth history, basically Codename 47 quality with the missions and stalking your targets, with several unique ways to finish, such as disguising as a pizza boy, etc...

It’s a stirring game, The Masterplan. Despite Marsh’s glowing appraisal of the Early Access version, I’d held back, slightly put off by the busy cartoonish graphics (I prefer my heists minimalist and clean), so I didn’t play until I had release code. The tutorial level, which holds your hand through the world’s easiest jailbreak, is a little clunky. It asks you to do very little but still managed to confuse me, although I’ll put that down to the text prompts that detail the instructions appearing so slowly that I rushed ahead and called the police to the site of my own jailbreak because I didn’t know how to punch a window.
While my own ineptitude and desire to hurry through the opening might be party to blame, I don’t think it’s a strong opening. As much as anything else, it combined with the graphics to convince me that the game was going to be a lighthearted series of romps rather than the cleverly constructed series of capers that unfold. There is a buoyancy to the ventricles but The Masterplan is a game in which you’ll frequently coerce civilians into violent acts and the threat of extreme violence and murder is your greatest weapon.
The ability to threaten people with a gun – real or fake – is what I’m going to concentrate on here. It’s my favourite aspect of the game and underpins a great deal of the other systems.
Basically, if one of your characters is in possession of a gun, you can drag a line from them to a point on the level to make them wave their gun in that direction. They’ll hold it in position, covering the area, and AI characters who are both in the area and have line of sight of the threat will surrender. At this point, they can be controlled by the player but if the line of sight or the cover-cone of the gun are removed, a circle around the threatened character starts to shrink and if it vanishes, they’ll run for the exit/nearest phone.
All of that can lead to situations in which you have one of your crew trying to cover a foyer full of people, the shrinking timers on each one becoming the plates that he must spin. The tension and desperation of crowd control is communicated instantly. Passing control of the potential victims to the player is a superb choice, converting them from annoyance to resource. I’ve created situations where two members of my gang are just far enough apart, across corridors and rooms, that I can just about force a civilian to dash between them before he regains composure and flees. I use him to ferry items between one and the other and as a distraction.
When civilians are used as distractions or shields, there is always the possibility of an accidental shooting. I don’t feel good about myself when somebody gets caught in the crossfire between my felons and the fuzz. In fact, I’m never happy when anyone has to resort to violence. My Masterplan doesn’t rely on murder or even violence. There’s always a Masterplan B though, and that occasionally involves a tripped alarm, a shootout in the guardroom and a death-dealing dash to the escape vehicle.
The Masterplan has more in common with SWAT 4 than with Monaco’s rhythmic arcade of colour and coin-pills. It’s a game built around cleverly designed maps and credible NPCs. The locations for your heists (unlocked by discovering flyers and plans in earlier levels) are convincingly real. NPCs arrive and leave, nip out of their office to go for a♥♥♥♥♥♥ and generally make you feel a bit guilty when you interrupt their lovable routines with the ugly promise of violence and death.
Thankfully, the game never becomes grim. That light-hearted cartoon style shows its worth, allowing the game to lean heavily on the cruelty of crime in its mechanics without ever tipping into grotesque displays of violence or pain. This would not be the place for such things – the game asks you to experiment and play with life so often that it has to retain the feel of a toybox. And it does so, handsomely. The panic of real-time control is countered slightly by the ability to slow the game down (practically pausing the action) but even in full flow, the game provides plenty of time to plan and think. Until an alarm is tripped or the police are called, most situations can be calmed while improvised escape routes are formulated.

First off, is it just me or is the entire launch cycle of the game UPSIDE DOWN? Even the main menu is upside down...
The game is very linear. If you walk past a "checkpoint" the game will not move along, you have to walk back to that "checkpoint" to proceed the mission. During my playthrough of this game, I met several npc's that spotted me and shot me through a solid wall when I was crawling along the ground in the bushes. They can also seemingly hit you with every bullet from over 500 meters away while looking a completely other direction than to you.
The story is very boring and the objective's in a mission is way to linear. So if the game wants you to go "THAT" way, you HAVE to go "THAT" way. And this happens as early as the very first mission. And there might be some npc's in your way, they are either dumb as a rock or smarter than Stephen Hawking knowing where you are before you've even entered their vicinity.
I ran many times into npc's that was just standing there while I was in their face without them doing nothing, just pointing their guns at me. Other times when I was completely hidden in the grass, they killed me with 1 shot from a place below me which was not visible at all from either points.
The sounds in the game is way to loud, and talking npc's can be heard clear as day even 500 meters away if you crawl past them while they are talking and if they don't have a set path to follow. This was very noticable in one of the last missions of the game. And the music pieces in the game is short and repetetive. For example during some stealth sections where ambient noises would have done it, the music from earlier just repeats over and over again.
At many points in the game when you want a vantage point to take out enemies, you have to climb up some stairs. That doesn't sound so horrible, but it is a challange just to get up the stairs since you will slide down them, and to climb them you have top either stand up and getting shot at or jump up the stairs. And if you see a ladder, it is not certain the game wants you up that ladder at all, you can climb up some ladders, but not all to get a good vantage point. And those ladders the game lets you climb up is not very good vantage points at all.
The game also changes from "sniping" to a normal FPS game with horrible recoil for the assault rifle's. The sniper rifle's recoil is manageable, while if you use an assault rifle it will jump a lot and screw up your shots. You also lift up your weapon if you are to close to an enemy, and then you either have to step back or melee the enemy. But the enemy will either just shoot you or melee you after you already started to melee him, and that is a 1 hit kill with just a bump of the rifle stock.
The game has a few good (or even great) stealth sections, but they are few and far between.
I do not recommend this game to anyone. It changes from a "stealth game" to an full out action FPS way too often with horrible weapons that is not a sniper rifle.

This entertaining and unique Texas Hold'Em game scores big points on most fronts, but the ridiculously stingy trial period takes some of the wind out of its sails.

Telltale Texas Hold 'Em was the very first game Telltale Games ever made. It was released just a year after the company's foundation date and before they got licensing deals to make games on pre-exsisting properties, they started off with an independent title. The game is a predecessor to the more commonly known "Poker Night" games. As common for most starting titles of a newly developed game company this game has its own share of flaws. There is no introduction sequence or a plot, after selecting "new tournament" on the menu you are immidately in position at a random Vegas poker taple with four other opponents named Harry Weinhead, Boris Krinkle, Theodore Dudebrough, and Grandma Shakey. Harry resembles a barber shop quartet minus three other barbers to sing with him, Boris is the bald guy with a "bad guy" look on him, Theodore is the frat boy, and Grandma Shakey is the elderly woman. All four opponents of the Texas Hold'Em tournament are ok. There is nothing too inventive or creative about them due to the fact that there is limited animation and amateur-ish character designs on all four of them. But if you look pass the flaws on the characters, the game is playable. It's not like Poker Night at the Inventory where there are awards and character skins to unlock. It's an average poker simulation and nothing more. All great game companies had to start off with something to get to where they are. And this game did help them establish new deals with other companies to create bigger better games. I can't promise that you will like this game, but it's only worth playing to see how much Telltale improved since they had started 12 years ago.

Join poker's most outspoken players for a hand of Telltale Texas Hold'em, the card game stacked high with personality. There are over 999999 other poker games, but this one TAKES THE CAKE! The graphics are amazing for it's time, the voice acting is so crisp and clean it actually improves your hearing and the soundtrack is better than Beethoven, DJ Khaled and IceJJFish combined. I liked the initial idea of Rogue Harvest: a survival game with permadeath seems like a fantastic combination, but I was disappointed by what the game has to offer. Here's a video of the gameplay if you prefer, which also demonstrates some of the issues I had with the game:
The UI/UX is very poor. The quick item slots are the only way to use items. They can't be used directly from the inventory. There are no hotkeys to access commonly used menus like inventory and crafting. For some reason there are only 5 quick item slots, even though they are activated by pressing a number on the keyboard. There should be at least 10.
The moment-to-moment gameplay is weak. It reminds me of Starbound in that regard, except it doesn't have the same level of depth and complexity to make up for it. The overall level of difficulty is far too low in Rogue Harvest. It doesn't feel like a struggle to live, so much as a romp through a fantasy adventure. I was expecting to die within the first 5-10 minutes. I was expecting to be slaughtered by the skeletons at night time. Instead, I was able to kill them without issue. The survival aspect is totally lacking.
The fullscreen option just stretches out the graphics to fill the screen. It doesn't preserve the aspect ratio of the sprites.
Rogue Harvest is in development right now, but I really think that the core gameplay needs improvement, and I don't know how likely that is to happen.

There certainly are places that I feel the game could be improved.
When I first opened the game, what popped out at me is the bobbing of the title. It was a very mechanical bobbing, with no ease, and is it just me or does the title logo seem like it changes when it changes its position?
The phrase "insert coin" in the menu of the game doesn't seem very appropriate, I was somewhat confused as to what to do at that point.
The sound effects in the menu were kinda loud and sudden, it startles me when I click on an option.
After I clicked play, I was loaded into... another menu? That was unexpected. That menu had a GUI that was inconsistent with the main menu, and perhaps even with the game itself. The mouse become an armored hand that I feel wasn't necessary, given that there doesn't appear to be a strong association between the game and armor.
The graphics seem inconsistent. The ground and the blocks do not share the same graphics. The ground has its own texture, and everything else are pixellated. Pixellation isn't bad, but if a game is going to do that, it should make sure that the entire game is pixellated.
I think that the description is somewhat misleading, since from what I gathered from playing it, players can't really build a castle, since they can't stack blocks. And the inventory and crafting is placed in a strange place, with no clear way of closing the inventory once open.
I certainly see potential within the game. It's very well-crafted, and very detailed. I do not believe there are obvious bugs or glitches, and the game is presentable. However, I feel like the game is somewhat inconsistent with itself. I give a list of things I found to be strange so that Genetix may be able to address them when updating the game.
Because this is Early Access, and not a final game, I do not feel the need to recommend nor the need not to recommend the game. Since Steam wants me to choose one or the other, it's not bad, and it can certainly improve, so I'll choose recommend.

I'm only 24 hours in at the time of this review, but I'm really enjoying this game. It is hard. It is grindy, but I like that about it. It feels like more of an accomplishment when you gain a level in a skill, because it took a lot to get that level. You have to manage your hunger levels of 5 diff food categories: meat, grains, vegs, fruits, and mixed in order to keep your stamina regenerating and your stamina has to be full to regenerate life. You start off building a base and before you know it you have a small little wooden walled area with a campfire and workbench and some baskets, soon enough you grow your base dominion stone to extend your area to 'safe' build in, and you can build a fence and a garden and some more sheds for storage and it just goes on.
It's not pay 2 win or to play. I think you can pay 4 convenience like exp boosters but I honestly haven't even looked at the cash shop yet there is no need.
The crafting system is very detailed I haven't seen such a detailed crafting system. For instance just to make leather armor you need to do so many steps like drying a raw hide on a drying rack, then soaking it in water i think in the tanning vat (the game at least tells you where to put what for each process), then you have to soak it again with lime liquor to make it supple, to get the lime liquor you need to melt limestone in a kiln/forge then craft the lime with clay and water, take the supple hide and use a bird dropping liquor or animal brains liquor to make it a soft supple hide, then you use tanning liquor and finally get a leather piece then you can make into leather stripes to use for leather armor or something else that needs leather. As you can see that is going to take a lot of harvesting of resources alone and then the depth to each thing is incredible, and that was only one example, making bronze ingots and stuff is also just as immersive.
You slowly get better in harvesting and crafting skills the more you use them and gets you access to better chances of successfully harvesting or crafting the better you get. Eventually with enough weapon levels you get combat abilities, I sitll haven't gotten any yet though, that's how slow the leveling is, which is great for someone who wants a game that doesn't just get extremely easy after a few levels and can have something to work towards. These skills are associated with stats, like strength, vitality, perception, intelligence, etc. that level up extremely slow which is great for having an end game and specializing your character to be better use to your play style. The slow stat gains really gives it an end game MMO character progression feeling in my opinion.
Still haven't done it, (have to get the process of making rope for a lariat going still, which takes spinners wheels and probably some other sewing type apparatus i would assume before I could actually make rope out of wool) but ive seen people riding horses and there are lariat for wolves, boars, and bears too so you can ride those too I would assume, which makes this game even better. With more players I think this game could really become a great MMO that people could look forward to playing when they turn on their system.
The game still feels very fresh at least on the english side there is not much to the wiki pages so its a bit of a hardcore experience, may be some things you will have to figure out on your own which should be fun but some people may not like that. It starts you off with a tutorial that teaches you mostly the basics and has you build half of a shelter then you run out of tutorial missions which is great you don't have any more missions but you have half-built wall and the other half is still wide open so you already have a mission even though it isnt listed anymore, and then the ball just keeps rolling from there.
Highly recommend this game

This is a MOBA game firstly, not a FPS even tho it is FPS based.
This is not an OVERWATCH or BORDERLANDS clone, it really is a hybrid FPS-MOBA if played correctly. The single player mode is like dungeon raids from an MMO.
Positives
1. The roster is big, very big, in terms of how different the characters are, potential builds, team strategies and what gear to bring into battle.
2, Teamwork is required in every game, if not you will die.
3. The amount of unlockable content is amazing if you're into what it has to offer.
4, Extra DLC characters can be bought with in game currency.
5. The campaign missions are quite long, and there is 8 (13 with the season pass), that makes it worth it.
6. Devs have promised short term commitment to the game (Summer - Winter 2016) in terms of patches, more characters and community events.
Negatives,
1. The Capture the Flag modes are awful, and it just feels they were added to boost the amount of maps. I don't like dominaton but it is the closest to TDM you are going to get.
2. There is not enough maps for multiplayer (where the real replay value is). There is currently only 6, but they are adding 3 more (one for each mode)
3. The progression rate for unlocks  is very slow, and the drop rate is overall low. it takes 40-50 hours to get enough gold to unlock any of the additional characters with in gaem currency
4. In game transactions were recently added for a currency to unlock better costumes
metics and other items. It's not game breaking but it feels cheap given the current game activity.
5. The community is currently quite small (<1000 people active) at any one time for a game that game out a month ago. This shouldnt be as such a negative point as many people say. I've been a part of many PC shooters (Loadout, Gotham City Impostors, Cod:AW, even Bioshock 2 multiplayer that thrive with small communities)
6. In my short time with the game, there is a lot of well experienced players. Like any MOBA esque game, you can get toxic players if you do not play with your hero/champion correctly. I'd advise to play a few bot matches with heroes to learn how they play and learn the details of maps, because they can be quite confusing to beginners.
7. There is still some bugs that need to be patched.
8. It does take time to get into matches
To conclude (to both potential buyers and Gearbox), this game's success is going to be measured on the commitment of both the community and devs to stay with it. You need to approach this game like a MOBA, where each person has a role in each game mode. If you lack the required support/defence hero then you might lose a lot. Im talking from experience.

bit Dungeon II is a Dark Souls take on The Legend of Zelda(1986). There are various bonfires with a few having merchants in the same screen.  There are 6 dungeons and a final dungeon consisting of two separate parts. There are 9 main Bosses and one hidden one, the Ice Golem. I have yet to find out what slaying this one does. On my second play through I noticed hidden rooms in bushes, but nowhere else. The enemies have great designs, though my favorite is the lanky, four-eyed monsters in the cursed forest followed closely by the dungeon cats. These cats show up in rooms you already cleared to tear at the remains of the fallen.
The over-world is quite small compared to The Legend of Zelda. Contrary to the main page, the temples are not randomly placed on the over-world. The dungeons themselves are fairly short and the bosses are simple and easy. I just stand there and hit them until they die, usually within 30 seconds. I have only died once at the hand of a boss. In fact I have only died 4 times total and have only one game over. The game is fairly easy and it only gets easier with high end gear. Since the loot is all randomized, I found unique items halfway through and passed on most everything else.
When first starting the game, there is a ghost of a woman who gives her soul to you for an extra life. If you die, you can return to the place of your death and reclaim her soul, very much like Dark Souls.
The second play through let me keep my gear and since the enemies don’t seem to increase very much in power, and the dungeons were exactly the same, there is very little replay value. I am currently on my third play through.
The game itself is short, a good 90 minutes long, if you don’t rush. Overall the game is a pleasant experience and worth the time for at least one play through. The 4.99 price tag is just about right, and I would strongly encourage getting it on sale or in a bundle if you are interested but are hesitant to get it full price.

I'm going to be "that guy" who leaves a rare negative review on an otherwise popular product. And I'm sure the fanboy children of the Jackbox community will automatically down-vote this review without reading or caring. Go on - do it. It's in your blood. It's okay - You don't know any better. ^_^
Honestly though, fans of Jackbox 2, hear me out.
Jackbox 2, prior to this version, was brilliant - I play it with friends regularly. It's become a tradition when we all get together. My disappointment with this new version stems from the lack of innovation. I'll break it down, game-by-game (the games that reduced my experience, anyway):
: When I saw this I was thinking, "aww sweet, some kinda Cluedo-esque game". It wasn't, sadly. What it was, was utter confusion. My friends and I, as bright as we are, couldn't figure out the points system, or why some people were killed off but came back to life, and so on. The game played us, if anything - we just came along for the ride.
:  This takes your typical Q&A platform and turns into a betting game of sorts. One player submits an answer in the form of a percentage (e.g. "What percentage of so-and-so love cake?"). The other players try to guess whether you're spot on, or think the real answer is higher or lower. The game, once everybody's has a turn to answer, just... ends... just like that. It was like, "uhh... okay! Moooving on..."
: We couldn't wait to try this, and at first it was a blast, combining art skills with lunatic headlines for t-shirt designs. Unlike Guesspionage, this game went on for faaaaar too long, with 6 of us anyway. The worst aspect of the game however is that it isn't the best design that wins, or the best headline, but the best combo of the two, which isn't decided by you. You don't design a t-shirt, team it with an appropriate headline. You mix and match with anonymous submissions from your friends. At the end of the game, one of my friends won the whole contest, because they teamed MY design with MY headline coincidentally, and I got squat. Yeah, no fun.
At this point we didn't bother checking out Fakin' It, or the rebooted Quiplash. The game had completely drained us.
As I said at the start - we LOVE Jackbox 2, it's fantastic. This latest, hottest version though just lacks logic, sense, true innovation and ultimately fun.

An attempt to create a humourus, Texas Hold'em experience, Telltale's rendition of the famous card game is painfully outdated.  Though poor graphics and awkward pacing is fully understandable from a game released during the early months of 2005, the dialogue is cringe-worthy at best, coming off more desperate than amusing.  The continuous commentary from the opposing characters simply feels clunky and unnecessary, forcing the player to click through the dialogue.  In addition, increasing the number of a bet, as far as I am aware, requires clicking the "Increase" button multiple times, as the game does not provide a slider to change the number that you wish to bet.
I have great admiration for Telltale Games' quality in their more recent releases, but this game simply is unable to keep up with newer, and cheaper renditions of Texas Hold'em.
Definitely pass on purchasing this product.

Very nice game for those who are curious enough to dive in the story, and seek to always find more and more about it. And believe me, if you are one of those, like me, you are not going to be disappointed.

In 'Her Story' you get access to a police database full of archive interviews with a murder suspect. There are a few clips to get started, but then it's up to you to unravel the rest of the story using keywords. You can use ones you hear in the videos, or try some that make sense. The story's a bit farfetched at times, but it's fun to piece everything together. Actress Viva Seifert does a really good job as Hannah. There's also a 'gotta catch 'em all' aspect to this game, where you just want to watch every clip available, to make sure you get the full picture.

An extremely simple concept, yet original and engaging. The idea that computers from the mid-90s were really awful is kinda funny - there's definately a bit of suspension of disbelief that's being asked of you here in that her interviews are hopelessly garbled and there's no record of the complete tapes (why were they ever cut up this way to begin with?) ... but then again, stranger things have happened with computers.  Anyway, the gameplay mechanic is fun, and this game pulled me in in ways most games don't.  Absolutely worth your time and money.

When you see the credits you ask yourself: did I really understand everything? This is not the time to find the answer on youtube video or website that contains magical trick how to unlock all the achievments - it is time to replay "Her Story". It is every criminal book-fan's dream game, that not only rewards your efforts of finding "keywords" with a great story, but offers you a pure joy of unveiling it, step by step - each more suprising than previous one. Excellent punchline is open to interpretation, so even if you did search the web for some explanation you are still not sure wheter you understand everything. Must buy, aspecially if you like indies.

Her Story is an engaging detective experience.
This is not a game, this is a case that needs to be solved. And you are the one digging trough the videos trying to get the clue. At times frustrating, thinking you have it all figured out, but then, you discover a new clue and you're not sure anymore whether you are right or not. It's a roller coaster of empathy. She will mind♥♥♥♥ you, without any regret.
8/10 would recommend to anyone that likes playing detective or likes psychological manipulation.

Pros:
- Different than the shovelware that floods Steam.
- Actually pretty nice system, albeit low on features.
- No micromanaging present in most other simulators. Relaxing.
Cons:
- Not as many features as could be possible in the future. Again, it's Early Access and I hope more stuff gets added.
- No options system, cannot adjust resolution or game settings. Not that it matters, since you can run this game on a microwave.
- No fullscreen windowed option.
- LOCKED AT 30 FPS.
Possible bugs:
- Science module can't be adjusted after setting research. Maybe intentional, maybe not.
- Scientist "people" disappear after the first night.
- Money doesn't actually update, making it impossible to actually get money in Career mode.
- For some reason the communication module doesn't show up on Creative mode.
- NO POWER icon shows up even with proper power. Doesn't charge the power banks.
Other noteworthy items:
- Low on features, not many modules. I blame Early Access.
- Nothing really risk causing besides research failures and loans. As long as you make enough to net a profit you can play the waiting game to increase your station size.
- Zooming out is with right click + scroll, which is pretty weird.
- Zooming out makes the stars scale out making the pattern very visible. I actually thought it was a grid system until I realized it was just the really big stars showing with the smaller ones disappearing. I'd recommend making a really really big star texture and repeating it less.
- There's a LOT of space to build a big station, assuming you can actually make it.
- I don't believe there's a way to deconstruct a module for better layout later on.
Overall: 3/10. Score will increase as more stuff gets added and more replayability. I'll mark it recommended because lots of work went into this.

Silent Assassin is the game that brought Hitman into the mainstream. It still holds up and is a massive leap from Codename 47 in terms of mission design, control and variety. Multiple apporaches to situations and sizeable levels with a good amount of unique secrets to find. It's suspicion/detection mechanic is a bit too strict, leading to enemies attacking you for no real logical reason, and many of the missions set in Japan aren't partically enjoyable in my opinion, but it's still a great game overall.

Hitman 2: Silent Assassin managed to successfully build and improve greatly upon the gameplay of the first entry of the series and mechanic wise can be considered the first 'true' Hitman game, featuring countless disguises and several different approaches to all objectives. Considering the time it was released it featured very large maps and successfully conveyed a feeling of absolute freedom to one's approach.
Being one of the earlier games, it didn't yet feature the massive amount of level and setting diversity yet and graphically, save for a few maps, was dominated by the colour grey, which is also probably a result of the predominant setting within Russia. All the same, Hitman 2: Silent Assassin remains being one of the best stealth games ever developed until this day and can therefore be heartily recommended.

First point of the review: This game has a free demo (insert rant on how demos seem to have mostly replaced by DRMs and on what that says about the game-making industry). Go play it. It's what sold me on buying the game.
I'd played a COG gamedemo before (Tin Star) and I skipped on buying it, as it didn't catch my interest. This game? This? I played the demo and when I reached the end I immediately bought it because I just had to know what would happen next. What happens next? It gets better, that's what happens next.
The NPCs are fun and believable (well, for superpowered people, anyways) - a few of them look stereotypical at first look, but most of those do reveal hidden depths if you befriend them and probe deeper. The story is great and hints of even bigger things to come. It gets slightly railroady at times (I still don't get why I have to be rude to Hi-Jinx, for instance), but that's unavoidable in a computer game, and there's no blatant plot-induced stupidity forced on you. And I probably chose the most boring path midway through the game. I'll have to replay it. Speaking of which...
This game has incredible replayability - with branching paths and mutually exclusive options, you'll have to play it about a (Diabolical) Dozen times to get all the information. There's half a dozen romanceable characters, too, if you're interested in that, of both genders, and they don't care what gender you are. And then there's trying to optimise the paths you've already chosen, which will likely lead to another couple of replays.
Fair warning, it's part 1 of, apparently 4? It's issues 1-4 of 12, so that's what I'm assuming. This means it'll take you some downtime and probably 4 times the stated price to get the whole story. The author has assured people that he's already hard at work on CCH2 and that he has no intention of pulling a Robert Jordan, a George Martin, or, heavens forbid, a Valve on us.
For those that care, you also get to suckerpunch people.
9/10 - if in a future installment I get to turn Professor Sleazemarble into a rockery, then 12/10

Bit Dungeon II is an action rpg rogue-like and hell lets also throw in there souls-like. Yes souls-like is a thing now. That means it is LIKE Dark Souls / Demon Souls.  The game is developed by KintoGames aka a fella who likes to call himself Alien.
Recently we did a developer interview on one of our affiliate partner channels
. Alien is a huge troll. Thus we had a great time. It makes total sense that he would make a game like this as these games often TROLL the player.  The video is currently being edited and will be up on site before long.
The first few things we noticed about the game was two very important things. Mobs respawn when you change screens, and you can full heal at the campfires you find.  You explore what seems like an open world that is partial randomly generated.  By that the overworld is the same. However the dungeons are randomly placed through out it.
Loot is random as well. It almost gives a feel of the classic arpgs such as Diablo or Titan’s Quest.  The art style of the game is pixel art and is ultimately what drove us to the game to begin with. Very  nice art style and very well done . The screen transitions and game play itself is very reminiscent of playing the older Zelda games.
Each weapon style has hits main attack and then a secondary special ability. Some weapons can be dual-wielded and some are two handed. You can find caves which grant upgrades to stats so be careful what you choose. As you kill you gain what appears to be soul orbs. You can use soul orbs as currency at certain points of the game should you find them to purchase more stats or rare equipment.
Each dungeon has a gigantic boss to defeat and the bosses are pretty unique and fairly difficult. However a ton of fun. The most important part of the game that stands out is… One soul. You die once, and have a chance to retrieve your soul. Should you fall again… Perma death. GAME OVER MAN! GAME OVER!
The games soundtrack is fairly decent but I found it to get fairly annoying if I played in very long sessions. Still the soundtrack fits the game very well and that happens few and far between in gaming these days.
The game is single player but I would love to see them add online mp or coop at some point.  It also has leader boards and steam achievements and here is to hoping for some steam trading cards. In all this game is a lot of fun and for the price of 4.99 it is a must buy.  We also want to point out that it is playable on Windows and MAC.
I had a ton of fun playing the game. Even more so during our chat with Alien. It was very amuzing. There were so many times I was fighting a boss and glanced down for just a second to read chat and ended up dead! YOU ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥S! It takes a lot for a developer to make a game that is meant to kill you but keeps people playing it. This game does that!

Is just that.
Stories."[/h]
And that line, in the essence, is what this game is about. I would guess that if we saw these seven interviews back to back, in order, this would be a pretty basic mystery. What makes this game unique, much like the movie Memento, is it's structure. It allows YOU, the player, to tell the story by searching words to find the clips, and then to put it together in your own head what really happened. This concept never works without a great performance by it's lead, and great writing.

Tagging videos ended up not being all that useful, but if you run it in windowed mode and take notes then you can get value out of them so long as you don't use any tag more than 5 times unless you add multiple tags with comma separations.

I want to start my review with this: Battleborn is a good game. Battleborn is a beautifully crafted game, with so much love that went into it. I can describe my experience with battleborn as a love affair that started passionately and ended with me broken-hearted. I, while loving Battleborn with all my heart, cannot recommend it to someone looking for a game with the pricetag it offers. Even at a lowered cost, I cannot in honesty recommend it to anyone, and that makes me sad. I've always told people to try Battleborn before claiming it worse than Overwatch, but I can't do that anymore. In its state, it is near impossible to recommend. Its player count seldom peaks higher than 1,100. Match times, while improving with updates, can still take 10 minutes with generosity. Battleborn plays beautifully. The characters are intricate. The story, while lackluster, is fun. Match types are unique (mostly) and maps are beautifully crafted (with one exception in PVP and one exception in PVE), and matches are fun. I have so much fun playing Battleborn. It is a good game. It is unrecommendable. I will try to squeeze as many hours as I can in game, but no, I will not recommend it.

I really like Battleborn and I want this game to succeed, but the game is having an identity crisis between wanting to be a competitive FPS MOBA and a Korean loot grinder. The PvP is so painfully inaccessible because you don't get gear from participating in it and barely get enough credits to cover the disgustingly high character prices.
Balance is in a poor state because it takes too long waiting for consoles verification, matchmaking has new players pitted against people at max rank (so they at least have more characters, gears, and mutations unlocked), and the game's "triple-dipping" monetization model isn't doing anything for the game's hemorrhaging playerbase.
Even though this game has quite a bit of flaws, and some of its aspects have not aged all that well, I can still recommend it to any Star Wars or Bioware fan that wants to have a good time.

This is the game I play when I'm feeling really depressed about the fact that I'm not a Jedi out to save the universe from certain doom, because we all know that most of really would like to have the opportunity to become a Jedi if such an opportunity existed. However, most of us make do with video games - and this RPG (one of Bioware's earlier incarnations) is still one of the best I've ever played despite it's age. The graphics stand up pretty well against the test of time, and if you're willing to look past it and into the story-line I think most players who have NOT played this game yet will find it worth their time. You can see Bioware picking up with some of the ideas that would become so popular in their later games (romancing your companions, funny conversations between said companions, choosing your perfect team amongst a variable of many, choosing a path of dark or light). The character customization system was not yet as sophisticated and the alien dialects when speaking to NPCs who dole out quests can get a little long winded, but it's Star Wars at it's best - a space opera played out against a backdrop of different planets/places with that age old struggle between Jedi and Sith as its star. Plus, you get extra points if you can put up with Bastila for any extended period of time.

KOTOR 1 was released in 2003, so its practically made for weak laptops
-The gameplay itself is based off tabletop d20 rpgs with the ability to pause the action to queue up attacks, so no fancy movement or split-second reaction time is required. Just sit back and watch your characters duke it out for you.
-The control scheme allows for the game to be entire played with either a keyboard or a mouse. Great if you have a terrible track pad, or you just wanna be lazy and play the game one-handed with the mouse.
-The engine's designed around comphensating for low framerates. When the game starts to lag out, it'll begin to teleport the player forward to keep the movement speed constant so the player won't notice how choppy it is,
-And setting the game to lowest settings kept my computer from getting hot at all, which can be helpful if you computer has a habit of becoming hot to the touch (I'm looking at you, mac users)
Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic is a fantastic Bioware game overall, and I'd definitely suggest it to anyone who's computer only seems to run 2D indie and DOSBOX games like mine.

Very fun game, However there are some technical problems on WIndows 10 (Just as any old computer game) , It is a very good game if you do some technical matenince. Since im a nice person i'll tell you how to make the game better.
The first problem is resolution, in order to get a 1920x1080 resolution you must find the game in Steam Libray > Steam Apps > Common > Hitman 2 Silent Assassin then open the "Hitman2.ini" file and it will open up as a text file, then scroll all the way down and you should see the text "Resolution:????" replace the current resolution and save the file, it should be in 1920x1080
Another problem people come across playing on new hardware is that whenever you Hold shift to run it will be very slow, this is because the game is going over 60fps, There is no frame limiter option anywhere in the .ini folder I mentioned earlier or anywhere else in the game. So, you will need another program to do this. Use a program called "Dxtory" it is a frame limiter tool, however it is not free but you are allowed to download it and use it in the trial version forever (The frame limiter is in the Trial version) CAUTION keep in mind that this is a program from Japan (It's in english so don't worry) so be careful where you download it from. They have a website I think.
That's it Hitman 2 is a very fun game, but it is old, and defenitely worth the $6.99, but before you buy it (If you want a good experience) be prepared to do some computer matienence, just as with any old steam game.

The story is about a normal person getting accepted in a a community college for future superheroes.  It's sort of like One Punch Man but you're only power is being the main character (which I definitely don't mean as a negative; you're just a normal person.)  You experience what any other superhero college student would: romance, friendships, weirdos in strange suits, evil villains and those weird classes you had to take to graduate.
Now, that may sound pretty boring or just plain odd but the way the story is written makes it very engaging and has you wonder what can happen next (and how you can not get killed by it.)  I'm anxiously waiting for the second part to come out so I can kick some super-villain butt with an electric baton and brass knuckles.  Doesn't that sound awesome?  You know it does.

Tagging videos ended up not being all that useful, but if you run it in windowed mode and take notes then you can get value out of them so long as you don't use any tag more than 5 times unless you add multiple tags with comma separations.

Summary:
Battleborn is a great game from the folks that made borderlands. It’s basically a borderlands take on a multiplayer FPS MOBA with some really cool gear and hero progression.  There is also really cool co-op “instances” which tell a neat story when played with others in a series. It’s a lot of bang for your buck.  The intrinsic replayablity of a MOBA game is greatly enhanced by the unlock system, rewards, and story.
While it is a Great game, unfortunately, this game suffers from head to head competition with the Marketing Gorilla which is the Warcraft funded uber conglomerate known as Blizzard. Due to this battleborn may not be able to maintain the player base it needs to survive in the future.
Battleborn Pro’s:
It's a REAL MOBA, it has ai minions, a form of junggling, and mercenary’s, it also has MOBA “like“ mode without ai minions just like Overwatch (if that's your thing).
It has a full single story co-operative campaign (think pug instances in Warcraft).
It has gear, usable in all modes, which you earn from playing!
It has a ton’s of unlockable hero’s which are unlockable by play and sometimes just given away. (alot of hero's awarded for first mission)
It has stories with great voice work in a Borderlands flavor.
Battleborn’s Con’s:
Overwatch "may" lead to an eventual death spiral of bleeding players...

Well, it has finally happened. After years of constant recommendations from friends and the broader community, I have played and completed what is considered to be the quintessential Star Wars game; a near unanimous masterpiece and supposedly one of the best role-playing games of all-time.
Was it worth it? Did it live up to expectations?
That big, blue thumbs-up should give you an idea.
There is so much I would like to say about
, but in such a small character limit. As already indicated by the thinly-veiled reviews, years of support and playthroughs beyond counting in more recent titles, BioWare is a developer I still continue to hold in high regard as a team that has delivered some unmatched personal favourites over the years and truly memorable experiences.
Knowing next to nothing of
and very little of Star Wars lore in general then, you can imagine the surprise of finding a video game that lives up to its enduring legacy and, even more so, the regret of not having played it sooner.
There will not be any spoilers or discussion of the narrative here, nor even a basic or general premise, suffice to say that it is
good - you should experience it for yourself.
What I will say however is that to be more than twenty hours into the first playthrough and have such a massive plot twist hit - completely unforeseen and unexpected - is indicative of the level of quality that
shows.
Building on the classic formula of design and narrative that would later come to influence the likes of
and
, the writing here is absolutely top-notch, as to be expected in a BioWare game. All the companions and party members are fleshed out and gradually present enthralling stories through a tonne of meaningful exposition... and romance, if you so desire.
Reminiscent of the many hours spent in
, the pacing and strategic depth to combat is remarkable and lightsaber gameplay is some of the best out there. A definitive step between the design choices of both old and newer games,
is heavily reliant on the many stats, factors and attributes that are running behind the scenes and a welcome reminder of the RPGs of yesteryear. Chaining abilities together is immensely entertaining, especially dark side powers, and carving through a group with lightsabers is just as good as it sounds.
As overwhelming as the recommendation may be however,
does have flaws.
Tactics for the A.I. are decent enough but navigating and establishing a set of commands between enemies for a single character, (let alone an entire party), can often feel clunky and slow to respond. Invisible walls are aplenty, (common for games of the time), but you will also find yourself stuck on geometry a lot - visible or otherwise - and temporarily unable to move. But honestly, these really are insignificant when compared to the game overall and, while noticeable, are hardly a problem. I had no issues with running it on a more recent operating system, though this initial save game was of the base (and unmodded) game. (They are coming up next.)
Also, if you have not designed or optimised your character class properly (or party, for that matter), it is likely that you will not enjoy the experience. As was already mentioned,
is heavily reliant on traditional dice-based role-playing and stat factors. A wrong decision in levelling and feat allocation could be unforgiving, leaving you with the option of playing with the difficulty settings or tanking it with health kits and buffs. Play to your strengths and build the party around that or check out one of the many build guides if unsure.
is more than worthy of the success and acclaim that it has earned over the years. A traditional epic in all sense of the word, the enduring BioWare phenomenon is definitely worth your time, regardless of your level of investment in the Star Wars universe.
This really is a timeless classic and undoubtedly deserves a place in your library. Recommended, easily.

The first thing I want to start with is that this game includes the Goldium Edition of the original mid-2000s Motherload. Motherload was one of the very first online Flash games I ever played - when I was a kid and when Flash games were still, you know, a thing - and I have very fond memories of it. For a Flash game, Motherload was high-quality and exceptionally deep (yes, a pun). And you know what? Still is. Honestly, this would be a pretty worthwhile purchase even if it was just the original game. It's still exactly how it was, slightly-awkwardly-Flash-based and with a few occasional technical annoyances (and boy, does it not scale well to full screen) but it's still highly, highly addictive.
Super Motherload I actually haven't played too much of yet. I had to revisit the original first, of course! But from what I have seen, it is just as quietly top-notch as Motherload was back in the day.
So get this for the original Motherload. Glory days. The simple joy of digging really, really deep holes.
But get it for Super Motherload too, which is a heartfelt, well-crafted modernisation of a classic. This is what all the old Flash games wanted to be when they grew up.
Very good trip down the memory lane :)

This game has great potential but also many flaws which can easily ruin the experience.
Do not expect some crazy hard game, it's quite easy instead. It gave me the impression it was made with kids as its main target. Mostly for the (italian) narrator voice but also because there a lot of checkpoints. A LOT. Even during boss-fights. This leads to an overall light experience, which can be a good change from those ultra hard games.
Level design and art style are without a doubt its selling points. Top notch. Colorful and variegated really draws you in.
What could let you down are some occasional bugs and faulty collision detections that may happen during your playthrough.
It also seems crashes are a bit too common. Have a look at the community hub as it has a lot of different solutions; I tried a few and I think it was
that did the trick for me.
If you're lucky and don't encounter any of the aforementioned problems, you'll be free to enjoy the variety of the levels while swiftly moving through them thanks to pretty smooth animations. I happened to run into what it looked like frame drops (not sure as, as said, I had Steam overlay disabled) during boss fight with lot of moving objects on screen (be it part of background or stuff to avoid in the foreground) which made it hard to fight and, generally, move. Luckily, it happened like twice in the whole playthrough. :)
What I found to be not good as the rest are:
- camera placement, which sometimes happened to be behind decorative objects who may prevent you to see Zack and/or enemies;
- changing suits, whose input keys doesn't seem to be as accurate as other keys (at least, if pressed during movements/combos. No problem if you only change suit)
Other small flaws may be found in translation (italian has a couple) and narrator (yup, again. Made me feel like a kid).
Found strange that there were no credits at the end, just a congratz message.. oh, and it clearly announced a sequel but I kind of have low hopes of it seeing the light, sadly :(
Achievement for completing the game may not unlock properly but don't panic. Last savegame places you to the very end and I read that just a reload may help. Mine unlocked only when I closed the game, after a couple of those reloads.
I've enjoyed my playthrough and want to encourage you to look beyond those flaws I've listed and give it a try. You now know what may expect you and it won't be difficult to beat.. I think you could end up enjoying it :)

Regardless of Zack Zero having a lame name, which I can only put down as a play on words and a hint towards the 'Ben 10' franchise as the game itself offers us no other reason for his name. Personally I found this game to be exactly what the main 3 developers at Crocodile entertainment...
Set out to produce and advertised it as, and that was to be a fun platformer dressed up to look 3d with a Saturday cartoon style about it all.
The fun aspects all stem from the fact that Zack Zero is a one man army with all the Mortal Kombat moves at his disposal that you could think of. Plus if he ever dies by falling off a cliff, you simply respawn with no loss to your characters gem and special item collection. So the whole adventure serves as a fairly stress free, lets blow all this kibosh up.
The story is that your girlfriend has got herself kidnapped by a very ugly looking relative of bowser. I really never thought bowser could look any uglier, but somehow he does. I guess in the evil lizard/crocodile/dinosaur/snapping turtle world fertility options are rather limited. Hence he kidnaps your girlfriend, he also holds her ransom for a chemical you have at your disposal which looks like something that would make Superman go hide behind the couch.
In Australia we have a saying, ‘If your girlfriend gets taken by a crocodile and her head doesn't resurface after three seconds. Go find yourself another girlfriend.' Zack Zero has a more beautiful blonde assistant at his side, and in truth I spent many hours of the game trying to convince Zack that this Marlene of his, who can't even bake us a cake like Princess Peach, is just not worth all the lava spitting frogs, the giant lobsters, the robotic spiders and all the other efforts needed in order to get her. The game constantly throws over 30 enemies at you through the various levels occasionally breaking up the action with small puzzles here and there which even a dog going to sleep on your keyboard could solve.
The game was originally designed for PS3 and then imported to PC and so it plays out extremely well with a controller. Its benchmark though is the developers attention to an imaginative, colourful world with stunning backgrounds, all of which are slightly inspired from one of the main developers earlier games known as ‘Phantis’ which can be found here...
Seriously how do you go from a rubbish game like ‘Phantis’ and then produce something quite extraordinary like this? They have my respect not just for that, but also because of the sheer guts and determination that they had to go through to get this product done in the first place. The game took 5 years to make in total, largely due to the lack of financial support that they received because the world was in a financial crisis at the time of this games design and banks were simply not lending out. Still they battled against innumerable odds, sleepless nights and risky financial letters to get this creation to us. A lot of heart and soul went into its design and that is easily detected by the sheer amount of illustrative detail into its artwork from the opening scene of the game right down to the very last scene.
There is 2 tally boards one which calculates the high scores which requires you to not only collect all the gems and special items in each level, but also to do it in the quickest time. The other tally board simply just calculates the time it takes you to get through each level using all of ZZ's special powers.
The biggest problem with the game to me is that the main protagonist really had no charisma about him, other than the fact that he knows how to blow things up. There are no corny one liners, no grandad jokes, no catch phrases or larrikin emotions which make him loveable. It’s like you control a cardboard cut-out with a rocket launcher attached. Likewise I had no invested emotions with Marlene his girlfriend and would have been more than happy to have dropped her pursuit at a drop of a hat. I tried desperately to convince Zack to swing the space ship back to his home world, plant his manly cardboard cut-out arms around his blonde assistant and sweep her away on a honey moon to a land free from Giant lobsters. Even the bad guys got more of a sensitive aww isn’t he cute out of me more than any of the good guys did. Hell even the invincible dodo chickens got more of a emotional response out of me than the main character did.
In final, a really stress free ‘let’s cause carnage’ platformer that leaves itself open for a sequel. If there is going to be a sequel then I want three things in it. 1) I want it not to take the developers 5 years. 2) Since a crocodile took my girlfriend, can we keep it Australian and have a dingo take my child? And 3) The Dodo Chickens in the game seem more invincible than my super powers can I pick them up and throw them around the place like a grenade at all the bosses in the game.
Thank you for making the game. Thank you for reading the review.

A great party game to introduce casual gamers, newcomers, or just plain anyone slightly interested in gaming to since nearly everyone carries a touchscreen device with internet access around these days and there is far less intimidation getting a group together to play Jackbox games compared to explaining button configurations and steep learning curves involved in other types of games. Quiplash can bring some pretty hilarious results due to players' responses and each game is unique due to each individual personality and thought process in providing answers. Trivia Murder Party is my favorite game of the lot and is well suited to a Halloween party; the trivia questions are hard and it's great to have a mode where even players who feel so far behind others in points can still comeback for a clutch win. Guesspionage is an interesting game where you will find out facts that you didn't know due to the fact that a percentage of people who do a specific activity will be higher, lower, significantly higher, significantly lower, or spot on to what you have guessed. Fakin' It is the more involved and active games where it requires you to hold "poker" faces and have timely reactions to ensure you are "fakin" it and blend seamlessly with the group. Tee K.O. lets you express your creative and artistic side by creating pictures and slogans that can go with a t-shirt; some player responses can make for some awesome and comedic results. You can even custom print a t-shirt with the favorite t-shirt design which can make some funny t-shirts you can rock with your fellow friends.

After playing the last two party packs I didn't think they could get any better, but this pack definitely proved me wrong. First off I would just like to say that I LOVE THIS GAME!!! Sure its a bit rough around the edges right now, but the possibilities are endless! This is not a game for everyone, and I will warn you that if you are not into survival games, REALISM, etc., then you need to keep walking right on by. This is not a game for those seeking an easy way to "Master" a game, quick payoffs or pay to win, but rather for those that like to work hard and feel a real sense of accomplishment when all the hard work pays off.
Just like in the real world, there are things we all need to not only survive, but to prosper. We need shelter, a bed, food/water, clothing, heat and cooking, weapons for hunting and defense, a place to put our things so that they are not stolen(storage), transportation, etc., etc. This game handles that splendidly with ultra realism! Everything that you have, you must earn through hard work, creativity, and experience. There is no "Just go to the store and buy it". For example, if you need a shirt, you have to "learn" how to make it...you have to gather the supplies, build the tools, keep it clean and maintained, etc. If you want to keep the rain off your head you have to learn how to build a shelter and gather what is needed. Think the hard part is over? Getting what you need is just the beginning! Now comes the trial and error of trying to make that shirt or the shelter! Tools can be broken, materials can be wasted/destroyed, etc. JUST LIKE IN REAL LIFE! Through it all, your avatar will learn and grow, and eventually things will be mastered and easier to construct. Just like riding a bike in real life, you may have fallen off, been injured, broke your bike, etc., but through trial and eror, you eventually learned how to do it and to perfection! And do you remember how gratifying it was once you had learned how to do it?
As with building, there is also a learning curve for your character and you when it comes to hunting, resource gathering, protecting yourself, etc. The more you do things, the better you get at them. Creatures in this game are no slouch either just as they are not in real life. You will not go toe to toe with a bear. You will not outrun a wolf. If you have to fight, well good luck!
Lastly, there are natural things you will have to contend with. Birds eating your seeds, weather killing your crops, starvation, etc.
So with all that said to give you an idea what you will be up against, there are a few other things that may turn you off or that do need some polish. I am sure many of these are in the works!
1- No map. Sure if I were stranded out in the wild in real life, I wouldnt have a map. But I would remember my surroundings, and eventually know where everything was based off landmarks...and it really wouldnt be hard to draw my own map. There would still be the issue of never knowing what was around every corner and what was waiting to kill me, but at least I would have some direction. The game has indicators that tell you the direction of home and your corpse, but that is it. Maybe in the future the devs will impliment a map making skill and map of some sort, or like in older games, have a mini map which is revealed more and more as the player explores. I personally do not mind not having one as it adds to the anxiety and stress level of the game.
2- Lag. This game needs optimization and some server work something fierce. The longer your play session the worse it gets. I find that I am reloading after every couple of hours which fixes the issue temporarily.
3- Mount AI. There is none. You can mount and ride and unmount....and if you choose, kill and loot resources. They do not follow you, protect you (those that should be able to such as wolves and bears), and there is no way to call them to your location after dismounting to do whatever it is you need to do (whistling for your horse, etc.) There are a RARE FEW that have an inventory icon that you can use to "summon" them to your location, but that is it. Walk to far and forget where you left your mount and well, your out of luck and have to find, catch, and tame another one. It is possible to find them again down the road as they will never move from where you left them. They do not eat, and there is no upkeep, but they do die if attacked.
4-Limited creature types, ore/gem types, and activities. I have logged a ton of hours and so far I have only seen 10 different types of creatures, all can be hunted and similiar resources gathered. This is all fine and dandy, just gets a bit stale after a while. Considering the setting is wilderness, I would like to see some creatures like mountain lions/cougars,  large birds like eagles and hawks/falcons, snakes and reptiles, and a fishing system with various types of fresh water and salt water species. The ore system now is sufficient dont get me wrong, but would be nice to see some rare precious/semi-precious stones and ores for a bit of flavor.
5- No age system, mating/children, hardcore mode. I know I know, all of you just went rated XXX on me. What I mean by this, and just to add to the realism, is to add an aging system so that there is a time sensative aspect to the game, and decisions made are even more critical. It would also open up other systems that could be implimented such as assigning chores to the kids, teaching them to hunt/fish, build, a trait system, etc. The possibilites are quite astonishing here!
6- Lack of players!!!! Its pretty lonely in the game right now, and only we the players can fix that. I have to admit though, that when I do see someone, my anxiety level and stress levels go through the roof! I play on the PvP servers and you just never know when someone is going to try and take you down!
In the end, the game mechanics and the systems used are as realistic as it gets. The game, just like real life, keeps the proverbial "carrot" dangling in front of you, keeping you going and going and going! As of now, the world is a bit sparse of players and interaction, but I hope that changes soon!
I highly recommmend this game, and I hope the Devs keep up the good work!

CUBE LINK:
~~~~~~~~~
Do you remember the days of the Magic Cube? For me it was about thirty years ago when it was at its most popular. I was mesmerized by it and spent endless hours trying to figure it out. I think my brain cells were not connected properly at this stage. Now I have a chance to redeem myself with this new game called CUBE LINK!
CUBE LINK is a casual / puzzle game where you have to connect colour tiles on cubes.
The first few levels are basically simple and easy tutorials. It will show the player how to connect the colour tiles and how to rotate the cubes. Levels will become progressively harder as the cube becomes bigger, in regards to how many tiles are on each side of the cube, and how many colours need to be connected. To give you a bit of an idea, it can become quite challenging when each side of a cube as twenty tiles or more and seven or more colours to connect with their own path, without crossing over each other, as fast as you can . To make things even easier, some of the tiles can’t even be utilized! That’s when your head starts to smoke and you wonder if you brain cells are firmly connected. If you are like me, redemption might not come so easily. For my part, I became well acquainted with the reset button.
Another fun thing is that you can lock the colour connection path if you feel confident that it’s the correct one. If it’s not, just unlock them. There are stacks of levels to play and unlock.
Graphically, it’s simply a cube with coloured tiles on a plain, coloured background. The best part of this game is how challenging it will become. In regards to the controls, you’ll be using the mouse, which is very responsive. The price is right.
Positives:
~~~~~~~
-	Clever puzzle game
-	Stacks of levels
-	Challenging, to say the least
-	Good price point
-	Achievements
Negatives:
~~~~~~~~
-	No trading cards

Decided to give this a shot along with Undertale to see if the hype and hatred surrounding it were deserved.  I figured if I really hated it I could always get a refund and get on with my life.
In short the game is quite an interesting little murder mystery in which you are tasked with studying the responces of a woman in a series of police interviews and using key words and ideas to dig up more videos, more clues and eventually the truth (or something like it) to the events going on.  Despite the criticism it's not pretentious and it's not this wierd feminist propaganda people claim it to be; it's just a simple murder mystery.  If paying attention to details, writing down clues and getting to  the bottom of a mystery is something you're interested in, I suggest giving it a try.  Avoid spoilers and internet trolls that pass judgement on games without knowing the first thing about them.  I gave it a try and I'm very glad I did.

A clever murder mystery game in which the player must search a database of interview clips for clues about the woman being interviewed. Each clue opens up new avenues for inquiry and pulls the player deeper into this well-written story.

This game is absolutely different than anything you played before. It can not be review in traditional way. First thing to say is that there are minimum of ingame controls. You type a word (or more words) in database search. After you searched it you will get videos where the word (or words) was spoken. You watch these videos and write down names, places, things or whatever you want to search next. You gradually reveals the story, associate connection. Because in database all seven interrogations are scrappy you must connect it on paper or in your head. This outside-game interactivity is what makes this game really special and different. You will really want to find out what happened to this strange woman.
If you just want to relax from ordinary games or just want to try something new I'm glad to recommend this beautiful masterpiece.

As a huge fan of everything involving the detective/mystery genre this was a must buy for me. I finished the game relatively quickly, not what I was hoping.
This game covers a lot which I didn't expect and it was a beautiful surprise. E.g. there are multiple 1-3 second clips of just her saying "Yes" and "No" and you can see how different they are by the way she stresses the words. Simply the variety of clips and the clever answers you really understand the character.
To sum up the experience:
- Didn't need a lot of notes as a person who read a lot of crime novels and such, so figuring out the ending was easy.
- Even though I finished it fast, the game is a bold step to try and I would like to applaud the developer for taking the plunge because it worked out perfectly.
- Also a big bow to the main gal (Viva Seifert) and her acting. (Congratulations on the Best Performance award at The Game Awards 2015, you deserved it.)

This is not a game for the impatient. In fact, you are like a detective, trying to unravel a complicated life/death story by watching as many videos as you can. It never drags on; actually, within the first 15-minutes of game play, you get to take a peek at the last video (in chronological order). Amazingly, if you are not a devoted detective gamer/reader, the underwhelming yet thought-provoking ending will strike you as a sweet surprise.
The game interface is pretty straight-forward. All the videos were shot and reproduced to match the feel of the times of the VCR and Windows 95. The lovely buzzing of the computer fans and hard-disk was the icing on the cake in terms of the A/V experience.
HER STORY is not a tremendous triumph in indie games, but it certainly deserves a niche for its innovative story-telling and no-nonsense execution. It is also a fine example of how multi-channel support for indie games can produce gems like this one (by watching the end credits).
Highly recommended, especially for those who are bored with too many brainless FPS games.

Con: Accidentally....."spoiled" it on myself by virtue of playing the game. The fault here lies etirely with the structure. You type a term or direct phrase and are linked directly to a number of related video excerpts. Old Gummy Joe here thought searching the term "alibi" would be a good starting point for exploring the case. I was linked to an excerpt coming from the very end of the interviews. bit Dungeon II is simplistic and addicting.  You play as a warrior who is out to kill evil demons in this top down Zelda like world.  Your goal is to rid the world of these demon like bosses in dungeons scattered around.  As you beat up enemies, loot will be dropped and you'll have to make a choice on whether to take it or not because as soon as you move off screen the loot is gone forever.  The loot ranges from weapons, shields, armor, and amulets to help you in your quest.  You also pick up coins which can then be traded to merchants for weapons, armor, or a chance to get a rare weapon.  You carry around a ghost girl who gives you an extra life and each time you die, you get one chance to get back to the place you died at and retrieve the extra life.  If you die before you get that extra life back, you're back to square one and all progress is lost.  That's where the rogue-like comes in.  The enemies can be brutal and if you're not careful you could find yourself sandwiched between knights and instant death.  That is one thing that needs to be fixed is enemy placement.  Sometimes while in a dungeon, you may enter a room and instantly be surrounded by enemies that hit for huge damage.  At that point, it's just instant death and really unfair.  Enemies should be spawned a little distant away so the player at least has a chance to react.  Also, if the Bow and Arrow seems very overpowered in the game.  Most enemies in the game need to touch you to damage you.  As long as you move around and shoot arrows you'll hardly take damage.  The game is a little glitchy and unpolished in some areas.  For instance, trying to move up towards a jump off ledge causes your character to spaz out and the jump animation to play.  I'm also not a fan of the music restarting everytime I pause the game.
Overall, the game is fun to play and definitely worth the price.

I bought this game because I wanted to play something that was packed with variety and action, as well as playing something like Zelda (due to the description).
